axis: esm2_t36_3B_lora_scaleup: production run at the proven config, matched to the previous finetune attempts' data/epoch budget, promoted via --push-to-hub
note: trial-072's exact proven-fitting config (--lora-layers-to-transform 10, batch_size=16, no gradient checkpointing, bf16, lr=2e-4/wd=0.2/output_dropout=0.2) - already confirmed decisively HEALTHY and the best-quality result across the entire sweep (median AUROC 0.8811, best F1 0.5974, beating even the mature esm2_t12_35M_coarse_go_terms phase's trial-053). This trial keeps that exact config unchanged and scales the data/epoch budget up to match 'the previous finetune attempts' - the esm2_t12_35M_coarse_go_terms phase's own long-standing seed_config convention (epochs=10, max_train_samples=12000 resampled per epoch, max_val_samples=2000), rather than trial-072's smaller 8-epoch/6000-sample health-check budget. Sizing at trial-072's real measured throughput (0.0588s/example): (12000+2000)*0.0588=823.2s/epoch * 10 = 8232s (~137min) + overhead (download, 10x small LoRA-adapter checkpoint pushes) ~= ~142min estimate; --max-minutes 170 gives a generous buffer without capping a legitimately-running full 10-epoch job. --checkpoint-mode every-epoch given real A100 dollar stakes (losing a ~2.5h run to a crash with nothing to resume from would be a real cost). --push-to-hub is set: this promotes to kelmoir/cafa6-esm@main, using the newly-added best-checkpoint logic (training_run.py now tracks best_val_loss/best_epoch across the run and, if the best epoch isn't the last one, reloads and pushes that saved checkpoint instead of whatever the final epoch happened to produce) - directly addressing the user's explicit ask for 'push to hub on the best checkpoint, not just the last one'. --run-diagnostic is auto-appended by build_notebook.py, so the real AUROC/F1 read on this larger run comes for free right after training, on the GPU, no separate diagnostic notebook needed this time.
